title: Breath of Fire
knowledge: In the 0x080483xx object handlers, field 0x64 is a Thumb state-handler pointer stored as address|1; write it as `arg0->unk64 = (u32)&func;` (agbcc's relocation sets the Thumb bit from the function symbol). Also 0x030023E0+0xA4 is a u16 game-state id: declare it as a struct with a field at 0xA4 (e.g. extern struct {u8 pad[0xA4]; u16 unkA4;} D_030023E0) so the codegen keeps the `ldr addr; adds #0xA4; ldrh` sequence instead of folding the offset into the literal.

agbcc codegen idiom for global + constant offset: a direct `*(T *)(GLOBAL + off)` or `((T *)GLOBAL)[i]` folds the offset into the literal-pool relocation (the ROM then shows `ldr rX, =GLOBAL+off`), while the original usually loads the bare base and adds: `ldr r0, =GLOBAL; adds r0, #off`. To reproduce it, route through a local pointer: `u8 *base = GLOBAL; ... *(T *)(base + off) ...` — this keeps the base symbol and the add separate (used to match sub_0801DE18/sub_0801DEE0, where offset 0x2B is ldsb'd). Likewise a 2D array `extern u16 T[][2]` with `T[0x81][i]` emits `movs r2,#0x81; lsls r2,r2,#2

In agbcc, initialization statement order matters even for constant global pointers: matched sub_08061860 by assigning scalar state = 14 before p = D_03004620 and p[3] = state (movs r1,#14 before ldr r0). Matched sub_08061880 by storing a call result in s32, initializing the destination base pointer, then casting the result to u16 before the store; this emits ldr before the truncation shifts. Hoisting all global pointer locals to function entry introduced extra callee-saved registers.

agbcc Thumb `x |= CONST` register-order trick: the natural source emits `ldrb r2,[base]; movs r1,#CONST; orrs r2,r1` (load in the result register), but the ROM often has `ldrb r2,[base]; movs r1,#CONST; orrs r1,r2` (constant in the result register). Reproduce it with a u8 temp and a comma whose first part depends on the load: `u8 v; p[0x42] = ((v = C + (p[0x42] >> 8)), v | p[0x42]);`. `p[0x42] >> 8` is provably zero for a zero-extended u8 load, so it emits no instruction, but it orders the constant materialization after the ldrb and makes the constant the tied operand. Verified byte-identical

agbcc Thumb small-function idioms verified in sub_0806B1B0/1C4/1D8/200 (0x0806Bxxx): 1) Interwork tail call of a value-returning callee: `s32 f(void){ return g(0x22); }` with `s32 g(s32)` emits `push {lr}; movs r0,#0x22; bl g; pop {r1}; bx r1` (return address popped into r1 so r0 keeps g's result). The natural `void f(void){ g(0x22); }` instead emits `pop {r0}; bx r0` and scores just off. 2) Byte-constant store ordering: for `p = D; p[3] = state; p[7] = 0;` the target ordered `movs r0,#state; ldr r1,=D; movs r2,#0; strb r0,[r1,#3]; strb r2,[r1,#7]`. Reproduce with a SECOND zero local declared

Verified sub_0804F988, sub_0804F9A4 and sub_08053420 byte-identical with extern void (*table[])(u8 *) and table[object[byteOffset]](object). agbcc emits the _call_via_r1 thunk automatically; an explicit call to sub_080A0774 is unnecessary. Tables D_080FD670, D_080FD5A4, D_080FDFE8 indexed by object bytes 0xCB,0x50,0x3B respectively. The identical-code suggestions can preserve the previous function's data symbol: sub_08053420 needed D_080FDFE8, not D_080FD5C4 from its suggested identical source.

Verified in sub_08068C30, sub_08068C0C, sub_08068B8C and sub_08068B60: replace early returns with a single s32 result local assigned in BOTH explicit if/else branches, followed by return result. Early-return forms inverted branch order and moved literal pools (scores1781,840,1820,1120). The explicit if/else-result forms matched all four byte-identically. Apply when the target puts the zero-result branch before the alternate call-result branch.

Byte table indexing shape: sub_080382D4 matches with extern const u8 D_081DFAE8[][1] and D_081DFAE8[offset+2][0] | (D_081DFAE8[offset+3][0]<<8). A flat u8[] declaration combines base+offset once and uses ldrb immediate offsets2/3; the two-dimensional [][1] form preserves separate offset+2/base and offset+3/base additions exactly as the ROM. Integer/pointer casts alone did not preserve them.

Leaf Thumb functions that contain a conditional branch in the ROM have NO `push {lr}` and end in plain `bx lr` (e.g. sub_0800DA78, sub_0800DF98, sub_08013B8C, sub_080140B0, sub_0804E648, sub_08016A24). This project's agbcc always emits `push {lr}` + `pop {r0}; bx r0` for any function with a branch (with -mno-thumb-interwork: `push {lr}` + `pop {pc}`; O1/O2/O3/Os all the same), even when the body otherwise matches instruction-for-instruction. So such functions cannot be matched with the available agbcc; they were probably built with old_agbcc. Don't burn compiles on C-shape variations (if/early

Identical-code suggestions can retain original data symbols and unrelated definitions. Verified sub_080077AC, sub_080077F4, sub_08007818 matched by substituting their actual table symbols D_080F5908, D_080F5A74, D_080F5A98 for suggested D_080F58C4; use target literal addresses to check.

Verified sub_080388C8: pointer indexing p[i] (including i[p]) emits adds base,index, but integer-address arithmetic *(u8*)(i+(u32)p) emits adds index,base. This matched two operand-order differences without register pinning; useful when Thumb adds has swapped source registers.

Full-width bitfields (`u8 field : 8;` and `u16 field : 16;`) prevent agbcc from folding full-width bitwise operations that plain `u8`/`u16` fields eliminate. Verified byte-identically in `sub_080958D0` (`u16 unk54 : 16;` with `(--arg0->unk54) & 0x8000` emits the ROM's `ldr r2, =0xFFFF; adds r1, r2, #0; ands r0, r1` before `& 0x8000`), and in `sub_08063930` (`u8 unk7 : 8;` with `menu->unk7 |= 0xFF` preserves `orrs` instead of folding to `movs #0xFF`).

Register allocation tip verified in sub_08097110 and sub_0808C7B0: when a Thumb instruction overwrites a register that is dead afterward, reuse the C local for the new role. In sub_0808C7B0 reusing the parent-address local for the last byte loaded through it produced the target ldrb r2, [r2, #6]. In sub_08097110 reusing two locals across consecutive bit tests reproduced their register assignments and matched exactly.

For adjacent byte stores where the ROM prepares the first field address, then loads a zero used later, then loads the first store's nonzero value, spell that order with a named first-field pointer and a named zero local. This matched sub_08086678 and sub_080866C4. In sub_080866C4 the zero local is s32 because it is also the second call argument, so the call reuses the zero register.

Verified sub_080966C4 byte-identical by splitting mode = D_03004F30[9] & 0xE0 into mode = D_03004F30[9]; mode &= 0xE0; the compound form loads the byte in r1 and mask in r0 before ands r1,r0. The single expression does the opposite. Similar use in sub_080967C4: name the bit test result before loading its branch default to preserve instruction scheduling.

For the coordinate sum `adds r0, r2, r0` followed by `strh r0`, verified sub_080921B8: declare the branch-selected offset itself as u16, do `offset += actor->unk6`, then assign `actor->unk2C = offset`. A direct sum always gave adds r0,r0,r2, and compound assignment with a full-width offset kept the result in r2.

Verified sub_0809A254 (petto_fire) byte-identical using a switch with default first and the state byte as fourth argument to sub_080352D0. Read the ROM format string: "%s:%d:petto_fire: range over %d!" proves the fourth argument, which m2c omits because it already occupies r3. Adjacent btama.c state handlers use the same diagnostic pattern. Declare sub_080352D0 as a variadic debug printf stub.

Verified sub_0808E038: when a narrowed byte store is followed by tests of both the narrowed assignment and the raw decrement, use a full-width bitfield for the destination and write `(field = timer) & 0x80` with a separate u32 timer. The assignment emits the explicit byte mask while the second `timer & 1` uses the retained full-width decrement. Re-reading the bitfield emitted an extra LDRB.

When an entity handler copies r0 to r4 and immediately duplicates r4 into r5 (`adds r4, r0, #0; adds r5, r4, #0`), using `r4` inside the conditional block and `r5` for a final tail call (or `adds r2, r0, #0; adds r3, r2, #0` when there is no inner call), declare a local pointer copy `Entity *e = arg0;` at the top of the function and pass `e` to the final call. Verified byte-identically on sub_0804D504, sub_0804D538, sub_0804D56C, and sub_0804601C.

In sub_0804FE90 and sub_0804FE34, ordinary u16 table indexing folded the odd halfword into an LDRH offset. For the ROM's LSL #1, ADD #1, LSL #1, ADD base sequence, use *(const u16 *)((u32)table + (((index << 1) + 1) << 1)). Both matched byte for byte.

For a state transition that stores a callback and then invokes it, assign the function to a local function pointer, store that pointer, and call through the same local. This matched sub_08055A98 and sub_08055990 and produced the expected _call_via_r1 and _call_via_r4 thunks.

Verified in sub_0804494C: *(u16 *)(D_030023E0 + 0xA4) folds the offset into the literal relocation. A global struct with a u16 field at 0xA4 reproduces the base literal then adds #0xA4 before ldrh and matches byte for byte. This also helps identify similar D_030023E0 field accesses.

Verified sub_08053324: when a byte decrement is stored before its zero-extended value is tested and reused, load into a u32 temporary, decrement it in a separate statement, store it to the byte, then assign it to a separate u8 local. The target stores r0 before lsl r0, #24 and lsr r1, #24. A single u8 decrement local narrowed before the store, while combining the load and subtract into one expression put the sub result in r1. sub_08052A34 matched the related store-then-test sequence with u32 remaining and an explicit (u8) cast in its condition.

sub_080A07AC is the Thumb signed division helper (it takes absolute values, accumulates quotient bits in r2, applies the operand sign XOR, and returns the quotient). In sub_08059FE0, agbcc emits __divsi3 for C division, but the project linker did not resolve that name. An explicit call to sub_080A07AC with s32 operands matched byte for byte.

Verified in sub_08068850: assigning a literal hardware address `(volatile DmaChannel *)0x040000D4` after a clear loop emitted the DMA3 register base LDR at the original site. Using `&D_040000D4` for the real MMIO address instead hoisted that LDR before the loop, changed allocation, and required an extra callee-saved register. Keep all hardware register writes and the control readback volatile.

Verified in sub_08051628 that repeating identical halfword store pairs inside the two if/else arms lets agbcc cross-jump just the stores. An explicit shared label changed where the alternate call block and literal islands were emitted. When a target jumps into another arm's stores, try ordinary duplicated C statements before writing gotos.

In sub_080106B8 the state byte at D_03004830+0x2D behaves as a signed struct field for clearing bit 1. The signed field kept the complement of 2 as a negative immediate built with a negate and preserved the global base plus field offset. A signed pointer cast instead absorbed the offset into the literal.

The actor's word at +0x68 is a byte-stream cursor in the 0x08025Dxx script handlers. Verified in matched sub_08025D04, sub_08025D20 and sub_08025D48: command operands begin at cursor+2, and the handlers advance the cursor by 3 bytes for a byte operand or 4 bytes for a little-endian halfword assembled from two byte reads.

Addressing trick for fixed-offset globals (learned on sub_08013568/13580/1359C/13498): do NOT write `*(s32 *)(D_xxx + 0x168)` with a raw extern array. agbcc folds the addend into the symbol reference in the literal pool (`ldr r1,=D_xxx+0x168`), which never matches the ROM's `ldr r1,=D_xxx; ...; adds r1,#0x168`. Declare a struct with padding and access a member instead, e.g. `typedef struct { u8 pad00[0x168]; const u8 *script; } ScriptState; ((ScriptState *)D_03003420)->script = ...;` — that keeps the base symbol in the literal and emits the offset as an add (or as the str/ldr immediate when it

Setting high bit of a byte field: `u8array[i] |= -0x80` lets agbcc CSE with an earlier `|= 0x80` (same low byte), keeping 0x80 live in a callee-saved register (extra push/pop r4) and dropping the `movs #0x80; negs` materialization. Write the field as a signed struct member and OR with the complement literal: `((ScriptState*)D_03004830)->unk2B |= ~0x7F;` (s8 field). Verified byte-identical in sub_0801F8E0 and sub_0801F964, same pattern as matched sub_0801F688.

Matched ClearItemSlotById (0x0801DCCC) confirms that sub_0805CF40 takes a 16-bit item ID and a pointer to a 16-bit slot output, returning 0 on a match and 1 on failure. The halfword slot table starts at D_0202DBD0+0x204. Keep the zero status local when reproducing the conditional clear: agbcc reuses its register for the STRH.

In sub_08032298 and sub_080322C0, declaring `s32 result = 0;` before the two calls, then assigning `actor->unk3A = result; return result;`, makes agbcc keep zero in r6 across both calls for the byte store while still materializing zero separately in r0 for return. Using literals at the store and return missed the prologue and register lifetime.

Not code. 0x080FBFE0-0x080FC05F is a table of 32-bit ROM pointers (0x080FBD90 repeated, 0x080FBDF8, 0x080FBDB8, 0x00000000...). read_data confirms: bytes at 0x080FBFF2 are part of the pointer 0x080FBD90; 'lsrs r7,r1,#0x20' (0x080F) is not a valid Thumb instruction. The disassembler split the data at 2-byte boundaries into bogus non_word_aligned functions. No C can reproduce this.

Part of the 32-bit pointer table at 0x080FBFE0 (bytes 90 bd 0f 08 = pointer 0x080FBD90). read_data shows the region is a data table of ROM pointers; the 'instructions' are the high half of pointers interpreted as Thumb, and 'pop {r3,r4,r5,r6,r7,pc}' is the following pointer's bytes. Best score 20 (98.6%). Issues: compiler generates `lsls r0, r0, #4` instead of `lsls r0, r0, #2` after `lsrs r0, r0, #1`. Tried u8, u16, u32, separate statements, `val &= ~1u; val <<= 1;` - all produce same wrong shift. Also register allocation: target uses `pop {r1}; bx r1` but compiler uses `pop {r0}; bx r0`. The shift logic is (byte >> 1) * 4 = (byte & ~1) * 2.

Best attempt (score 440) is the if-form: `u16 *base=(u16*)0x03002AB0; u32 result=1; if (base[1]==arg0) result = base[3]!=arg1; return result;`. It is instruction-for-instruction identical to the target except register allocation: target keeps arg1 in r4, base in r3, result in r2, and emits `movs r2,#1` AFTER `ldrh r1,[r3,#2]`; best attempt gives arg1 r4 but base r2/result r3 and `movs r3,#1` before the ldrh. Tried: logical-or form (1040), if-form (440), result declared first + `arg1 != base[3]` (450), early-return form (875), result-first with `base[3] != arg1` (450). Remaining diff is pure register choice of the base pointer vs the result variable, plus one scheduling slot. Next idea: pin with `register u32 result asm("r2")` (then base should take r3), or try a struct-typed extern D_03002AB0 with .unk2/.unk6 field accesses so no base local exists. Note D_03002AB0 is a real project symbol (extern struct works); target loads its address into a register then uses offsets 2 and 6.

The C is right; the only remaining diff is 2 instructions belonging to the next function. Claimed 48-byte extent runs past the real end: code + 3 literals end at 0x08008A30, and bytes 0A 48 00 78 at 0x08008A30 are the next function's `ldr r0,[pc,#0x28]; ldrb r0,[r0]`, which the disassembler merged. Boundary reported (end=0x08008A30); recompiling still scores 200 because it is not approved yet. Nothing in the C can remove those 2 target instructions.

Best: score 210 (12/12 insns). Remaining diff: target does `movs r1,#4; ldr r0,=0x03004620; strb r1,[r0,#3]` (address in r0, value in r1); all plain C forms give the opposite allocation (`ldr r1,=addr; movs r0,#4; strb r0,[r1,#3]`). Tried: struct object member (u8), u8 array index, packed struct, u8:8 bitfield, local pointer assigned after calls, `&D_03004620 + 3` (folds into symbol+3 relocation, wrong literal), volatile u8 array (gets the right store order/regs but inserts a spurious `ldrb r1,[r0,#3]` read first, score 400). Hint: a volatile read-modify-write path (store_bit_field) produces exactly the target's write sequence, so the original lvalue likely goes through store_field without needing the read — try a u8-typed value variable with a volatile lvalue, or a packed bitfield, or a register-pinned pointer. Callees: sub_08060C7C, sub_0805B180 (void), function returns 0 (epilogue `movs r0,#0; pop {r1}`).

Same idiom as sub_08061E64: calls sub_0805B198, sub_0805B6A4, sub_08060C7C, then `movs r1,#2; ldr r0,=0x03004620; strb r1,[r0,#3]`, returns 0. Best 210; every plain form (struct member/array/packed/u8:8 bitfield/local pointer) allocates value in r0 and address in r1, the target is the reverse. Volatile lvalue gets the right store but adds a spurious `ldrb r1,[r0,#3]` first. See sub_08061E64 notes for the full list of variants tried.

Best score 200 (95.3%) with goto version. First 41 of 43 instructions match perfectly. Missing 2 instructions at end (`push {lr}`, `ldr r1, [pc, #0x14]`) are actually the NEXT function's prologue (0x00B5 0x0549 = push {lr}; ldr r1,[pc,#0x14]) - diff alignment off because tool thinks this function has 43 insns but actual body has 41. Core logic matches: control flow, calls, register usage (r4/r1) all correct. Tried explicit labels (worse regalloc), passing arg to sub_08068AF4 (wrong). Function effectively matched; boundary detection issue.

Cannot get closer: the project's symbol size is wrong (68 bytes / ends 0x0807E5F0), while the real function is 84 bytes and includes its own else block at 0x0807E5F0 (reached by the beq at 0x0807E5B2, uses this function's saved lr via pop {r0}; bx r0). The full if/else C (see my previous note) compiles byte-identically to the entire ROM function: if-body, pool at 0xE0, else block at 0xF0, pop/bx at 0xFA, pool at 0x0807E600. compile_and_diff can only compare the 68-byte window, so it flags the real else block/epilogue/second pool as 13 extra; report_boundary(0x0807E600) is rejected because 0x0807E600 is not inside the 68-byte symbol. Fix needed: set sub_0807E5AC's size to 0x54. Do not trust the saved no-else best attempt (832): it only fits the truncated window.

antigravity-gemini-3.8-flash-high-1.why: Function executes swi 171 (0xAB - Angel semihosting call) directly, which requires inline assembly in C. Since inline assembly is disallowed in C matching, pure C cannot produce this instruction.

antigravity-gemini-4-hydrogen-high-1.why: Contains swi #171 (0xAB, Angel semihosting SWI), which in newlib syscalls is emitted via inline assembly (__asm volatile("swi 0xab")) and cannot be generated by pure C without inline asm.

opencode-deepseek-v4.1-flash-free-1.why: Body is a straightforward 3-arg syscall wrapper (push {r4,r5,lr}; sub sp,#0xc; r4=arg1; r5=arg2; bl sub_080A44FC; str ret,[sp]; str arg1,[sp,#4]; str arg2,[sp,#8]; movs r3,#5; mov r0,r3; mov r1,sp; swi #171; return r0). Everything except the SWI is producible from C, but the ROM executes `svc #0xab` (Angel semihosting SWI 171) inline, which in newlib is emitted only via inline assembly (`__asm volatile("swi 0xab")`). agbcc has no builtin that emits SWI, and inline asm is not allowed, so no pure C can match. Other agents noted the same. This is newlib's _swiwrite/_swiopen-style syscall stub; mark as not C (or match with hand-written assembly in the project's asm form). Tested C: `fd=sub_080A44FC(arg0); return fd+arg1+arg2;` gives 1140 and cannot reach the svc.
